Work in the reduction conventions of
[[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]]: $\gamma$ is the signature
$(+---)$ metric, $U$ the unit future timelike vector $U=n$, $r=\rho c^2$, the
frame $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is $\gamma$-orthonormal with $e_0=U$,

**(a) Schouten tensor.** The **reduction Schouten tensor** of $\gamma$ is
$$S_{ij}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ij}-\tfrac16S_\gamma\,\gamma_{ij},$$
where $\operatorname{Ric}$ and $S_\gamma=\gamma^{ab}\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ are
the Ricci tensor and scalar curvature of $\gamma$
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). If the dust field equation
$G(\gamma)-\Lambda\gamma=\kappa\,r\,U^\flat\otimes U^\flat$ holds, then
$$S_{ij}=\kappa r\Bigl(U_iU_j-\tfrac13\gamma_{ij}\Bigr)-\tfrac13\Lambda\,\gamma_{ij}.$$
This normalization is fixed so that the standard Kulkarni--Nomizu decomposition
$$R_{ijkl}=C_{ijkl}+\tfrac12\bigl(S_{ik}\gamma_{jl}-S_{il}\gamma_{jk}+S_{jl}\gamma_{ik}-S_{jk}\gamma_{il}\bigr)$$
holds for every metric of dimension four, with $C$ the Weyl tensor
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]); the identity is checked on
constant-curvature metrics in the Remarks.

**(b) Prescribed curvature.** The **prescribed curvature tensor** of a
configuration $(C,E,B,r)$ is the tensor field with frame components
$$R^{\mathrm{pre}}{}_{ijkl}:=C_{ijkl}+\tfrac12\bigl(S_{ik}\gamma_{jl}-S_{il}\gamma_{jk}+S_{jl}\gamma_{ik}-S_{jk}\gamma_{il}\bigr),\qquad S_{ij}\text{ as in (a)} ,$$
where $C=C[E,B]$ is the Weyl tensor reconstructed from the electric and
magnetic variables in (d). A **tentative reduced configuration** is a smooth assignment
$(e_a{}^\mu,\Gamma_a{}^i{}_j,E_{ij},B_{ij},r)$ in the gauge of
[[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]]. Equality of its actual curvature
with $R^{\mathrm{pre}}$ is the curvature constraint, rather than an assumption
on the independent unknowns. Reduced evolution enforces its time components;
the residual theorem establishes the remaining components from constrained
initial data. This distinction keeps the tentative connection available before
torsion-freeness and the full curvature constraint are proved.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
signature $(-+++)$ and metric-selected connection $\nabla$. Fix mathematical
parameters $c>0$, $\kappa>0$ and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$. On an open set
$U_0\subseteq M$, prescribe a smooth function $\rho\ge0$ and a smooth
future-directed unit timelike field $u$, with $g(u,u)=-1$. Set
$\varepsilon:=\rho c^2$ and $T^{ab}:=\varepsilon u^au^b$. On the open positive
subset $\{\rho>0\}$, the tuple $(\varepsilon,u)$, rather than $(\rho,u)$, is
exactly the dust model of [[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]: that supplier's density
is the coefficient of $u\otimes u$. Here $\rho$ denotes its mass-normalized
parameter and $\varepsilon$ its energy-normalized coefficient. On zero-density
regions the smooth unit field is prescribed separately; the geodesic equation
is imposed there as well and is not deduced from conservation of the zero
tensor. This is the smooth geodesic-dust extension, without a free boundary
or a division by density. Make the following
**reduction conventions**, all local to an open set $\mathcal U\subseteq U_0$:

**(a) Signature flip.** Put $\gamma:=-g$, a smooth metric of signature
$(+---)$ on $\mathcal U$, with inverse $\gamma^{-1}=-g^{-1}$; all indices in the
reduction are raised and lowered with $\gamma$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]). Put
$$U:=u,\qquad r:=\rho c^2 .$$
Then $\gamma(U,U)=1$. Whenever the mathematical model equation
$G(g)+\Lambda g=\kappa T$ holds, it reads
$G(\gamma)-\Lambda\gamma=\kappa\,r\,U^\flat_\gamma\otimes U^\flat_\gamma$ with
the same constant $\kappa$ and the Einstein tensor of $\gamma$
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Indeed the constant metric
flip leaves the connection and mixed curvature unchanged, so Ricci is unchanged,
the scalar changes sign and $G(\gamma)=G(g)$; both lower factors in $T$
change sign together. The original metric is recovered by $g=-\gamma$.

**(a) Second-derivative inequality.** Let $\gamma:J\to U$ be a geodesic and
let $f:J\to\mathbb R$, $f(t):=|x(\gamma(t))|_{\mathrm e}^2$, where the norm is

$\sum_{i,j}\Gamma^a{}_{ij}(x)\dot x^i\dot x^j$ and $\cdot$ is the Euclidean
scalar product. Consequently, along every geodesic whose image lies in a
fixed compact $K\subseteq U$,
$$f''\ge 2\bigl(1-\|\Gamma\|_K\,|x(\gamma)|\bigr)\bigl|\dot x\bigr|_{\mathrm e}^2 .$$
In particular, if $x(K)\subseteq B_{r_1}$ and $\|\Gamma\|_K\,r_1\le\tfrac12$
then $f''\ge|\dot x|_{\mathrm e}^2\ge0$ at every parameter of such a
geodesic.

is contained in a compact $K$ with $x(K)\subseteq B_{r_1}$ and

$$|x(\gamma(t))|_{\mathrm e}\le r_2\qquad\text{for every }t\in[0,1].$$

The representing fields $N,N'$ themselves need not agree there. By steps 4.2-4.3, $Q$ is a Hausdorff second countable smooth manifold. Under Countable Choice, a subordinate smooth partition $(\rho_M,\rho_{M'})$ for its two-member open cover exists by [[thm-smooth-partitions-of-unity-exist-on-manifolds]]. By [L4] that portion is inextendible in the member and hence meets its Cauchy surface, so the whole curve meets $\bar j(\Sigma)$ at least once. For uniqueness, the sets $Q^\pm=p_M(I_M^\pm(\Sigma))\cup p_{M'}(I_{M'}^\pm(\Sigma'))$ are open and disjoint, and $Q=Q^-\sqcup\bar j(\Sigma)\sqcup Q^+$: this follows from the member side decompositions and their agreement on the common subdevelopment by causal convexity and future cone preservation. The surface is closed since its trace in each open member image is the closed member Cauchy surface. Near any surface point a future causal curve crosses from the past side to the future side, and has at most one local parameter visit, by a spacelike slice chart and strict temporal-coordinate increase. Thus the set of surface visits in a compact parameter interval is closed and locally isolated, hence finite. If two visits existed choose consecutive ones $t_1<t_2$. Therefore there is exactly one visit. [step 3.1, step 5.1, step 6.1, L2, L3, L4, contradiction, algebra]

- **Focusing versus singularities.** The Raychaudhuri theorem of this page is
  a local differential inequality along one flow line of a smooth geodesic
  congruence: it bounds the affine parameter range on which the congruence
  remains smooth under the stated hypotheses. It does not assert that the
  spacetime ends, that a singularity theorem holds, or that an
  infinite-curvature point forms. A genuine singularity theorem requires its
  own energy, causality and global compactness hypotheses and a complete
  proof, none of which is claimed here; cosmic censorship and chronology
  protection are not theorems and are not used.

- **Observer.** An observer at $p$ is one future-directed unit timelike vector
  $n\in T_pM$, $g_p(n,n)=-1$
  ([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]). It carries no parametrized curve and no
  clock reading by itself.
- **Congruence.** An observer congruence on an open set $U$ is a smooth field
  $n$ whose value at every point is an observer; its maximal integral curves
  are its observer curves, and its flow parameter is not a physical time
  ([[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]).
- **Frame and coordinate frame.** A local frame field is a tuple of four
  pointwise independent smooth vector fields; the coordinate frame of a smooth
  chart is the special case of the fields $\partial/\partial x^a$, whose
  members pairwise commute. A frame whose members do not commute is therefore
  not the coordinate frame of any chart
  ([[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]).
- **Tetrad.** A tetrad field is a pointwise $g$-orthonormal frame field; it is
  future-directed when its first member is future-directed, and it is adapted
  to a congruence $n$ when that first member equals $n$. A tetrad field need
  not be a coordinate frame. Local existence near every point is proved on this
  page; global existence on $M$ is not asserted and would be a nontrivial
  parallelizability property of the manifold.
- **Adapted chart.** A chart is $n$-adapted when its spatial coordinates are
  constant along the integral curves of $n$; one exists near every point of a
  congruence, by the existence corollary on this page, but it is not unique and
  its coordinate field need not equal $n$
  ([[cor-gr-adapted-chart-existence]]).
- **Rest spaces and their integrability.** The rest spaces $n_q^{\perp}$ of a
  congruence always form a smooth rank-$3$ distribution, and they are tangent
  to local hypersurfaces exactly when $\alpha\wedge d\alpha=0$ for
  $\alpha=n^{\flat}$. Thus an adapted chart always exists, while an orthogonal
  rest-space foliation need not
  ([[prop-gr-rest-space-integrability-criterion]]).
- **Components.** Coordinate components of a tensor field transform by
  products of chart Jacobians
  ([[lem-gr-tensor-component-transformation-law]]), while its components in
  two future-directed tetrads are related by a matrix
  $\Lambda$ with $\Lambda^{\mathsf T}\eta\Lambda=\eta$ and
  $\Lambda^0{}_0>0$ ([[lem-gr-tetrad-change-of-basis-is-lorentz]]). The two
  component systems are different data
  ([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]).
- **Observer-relative quantities.** Observer energy, spatial momentum and
  rest mass are defined with respect to a chosen observer; different observers
  generally assign different energies to the same tangent vector, and no
  observer-independent split of a tangent vector into energy and momentum is
  asserted ([[def-gr-observer-relative-energy-and-momentum]]).
- **Physical readings.** The interpretation of these geometric objects as
  observers, reference frames, clocks, particles and measured energies belongs
  to the physical postulates and unit conventions of the framework, recorded
  elsewhere on this track; the items on this page assert no measurement,
  dynamics or claim about nature.

**Signs and index order.** The curvature operator, the component order and the
lowered, Ricci, scalar and Einstein contractions are fixed once in
[[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]] and used unchanged throughout
this page: $R(X,Y)Z=\nabla_X\nabla_YZ-\nabla_Y\nabla_XZ-\nabla_{[X,Y]}Z$ and
$R(\partial_c,\partial_d)\partial_b=R^a{}_{bcd}\partial_a$, so that the
algebraic symmetries of [[thm-gr-curvature-algebraic-symmetries]] and the
divergence identity $\nabla^aG_{ab}=0$ of
[[thm-gr-second-bianchi-and-divergence-free-einstein]] hold in exactly the
displayed form. Sources that order the loop indices differently, or that use
the opposite overall sign, state the same mathematics in another convention;
no formula is imported from a source without converting it to this one.

**Units.** In length coordinates, in which $x^0=ct$ and all $x^a$ carry
metres and the metric components are dimensionless
([[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]), the Christoffel symbols
$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}$ have units of inverse length and the components
$R^a{}_{bcd}$, $R_{abcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ and $S$ have units of
inverse length squared. The Einstein tensor has the same units as the Ricci
tensor, and the field-equation coupling of the framework is normalized so
that $\kappa T_{ab}$ has the same units; no numerical value of any constant
is asserted by these conventions. In other coordinates, such as charts with
an angular coordinate, individual component units change with the Jacobian
and carry no universal dimension; only invariant statements, proper times and
observer-relative quantities keep their physical reading.

**Connection artifacts versus curvature.** The Christoffel symbols are chart
functions and not tensor components; a chart can make all of them vanish at a
point ([[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]]) without
making the curvature vanish there:
[[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (c) shows
that curvature at a point is exactly the second-order metric information that
no coordinate choice can remove. Conversely a chart may have nonzero
Christoffel symbols everywhere while the curvature vanishes identically, as
for flat space in curvilinear coordinates. Curvature is also not a trace of
itself: $\operatorname{Ric}=0$ is a weaker condition than $R=0$, and the
converse implications are not asserted anywhere on this page.

- **Matter sectors.** The matter content is one of the sectors of clause (iii)
  of [[post-gr-classical-gravitational-action]]: the scalar-field model with a
  supplied action and Hilbert tensor in the action presentation, or the dust
  and perfect-fluid models with prescribed stress-energy tensor and matter
  equations in the direct-equation presentation. The stress-energy
  tensor occupies the slot defined in [[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]];
  its component reading in a $g$-orthonormal frame is in
  $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$, and the coupling satisfies
  $\kappa T\sim\mathrm m^{-2}$ with $\kappa=8\pi G_N/c^4$ in the conventions of
  [[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]. The equation of state of a
  fluid sector is a further assumption of that model; the energy conditions of
  [[def-gr-energy-conditions]] are optional additional assumptions unless a particular matter model
  implies them; the field equation alone does not universally force them.

- **The bridge is a controlled comparison of models.** The weak-field results
  of this page — the Einstein and stress hierarchy
  ([[thm-gr-weak-field-einstein-stress-hierarchy]]), the geodesic
  acceleration estimate ([[lem-gr-weak-field-geodesic-acceleration]]) and
  the scaled trajectory convergence
  ([[thm-gr-weak-field-scaled-trajectory-limit]]) — are estimates inside an
  explicitly hypothesized family of spatially factored stationary metrics
  ([[def-gr-stationary-weak-field-data]]). Their hypotheses are essential: an
  existing Einstein family with the stated derivative bounds, the
  slow-motion condition $|\dot x|\le C\sqrt\varepsilon c$, a common compact
  spatial region, a comparison motion that exists on the whole finite scaled
  interval and a bounded second derivative of the potential. The Poisson
  source match to dust rest-mass density additionally assumes the stated
  nonnegative dust model, its conservation equations, weak-source bound and
  slow tilt. The page does not
  construct the input family from Newtonian initial data, does not prove
  existence of a global Newtonian limit in any gauge, and does not treat
  strong fields, fast motion, long times or non-smooth sources.

- **The displayed spatial form is chart-dependent.** The perturbation form
  $g_{00}=-(1+2\Phi/c^2)$, $g_{ij}=(1-2\Phi/c^2)\delta_{ij}$ is a statement
  in the chart of the ansatz. Under a change of chart the components
  transform by the covariant transformation law
  ([[lem-gr-covariant-two-tensor-transformation-law]]), so comparisons of
  spatial coefficients computed in different charts — for instance the
  areal-radius forms used in the spherical model — require the explicit
  coordinate conversion and are not identities; that conversion is deferred
  to the spherical-model page. Similarly, the gauge transformation of the
  flat linearization is a change of perturbation inside a fixed chart and is
  not a change of chart.

This page contains the Gr14 high-regularity symmetric hyperbolic proof material:
the periodic first-order theory (E0), the harmonic-gauge reduced Einstein
equation and its subsidiary system (E1), the geometric data and local
development theorems (E2), and the selected matter reductions with the complete
geodesic-dust residual chain (E3, E3d--E3d.2). Its content assumes Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) for local analytic extraction and manifold patching, and Dependent Choice ([[def-dependent-choice]]) for the causal-curve calculus in the Cauchy-neighborhood argument. Its physical content is conditional:
the physical reading is the model deduction of
[[pthm-gr-high-regularity-local-development]] from the adopted postulates
[[post-gr-einstein-field-law]] and the matter definitions
[[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]], [[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]],
[[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]; the mathematical carriers are
[[thm-gr-high-regularity-selected-matter-development]] and its prerequisites.

**What is not established or assumed away.** No global or all-time existence,
no uniform existence time on noncompact data, and no maximality or boundary
behaviour of the spacetime development (that is the scope of the successor
page). The matter results do not treat shocks, nonsmooth free boundaries,
nonsmooth vacuum interfaces, junction conditions, distributional or
low-regularity sources, or boundary layers; the theorem works in the
smooth/high-regularity branch with $s\ge5$ and makes no optimal Sobolev
threshold claim. These exclusions are distinct from smooth zeros of the dust
density. For dust, the construction occurs before flow crossings and a smooth
future unit velocity is prescribed and remains geodesic even where the smooth
nonnegative energy coefficient $\varepsilon$ vanishes. Thus smooth zero sets
and open empty regions are included, with no division by density. The source
density parameter is $\varepsilon$, with mass-normalized
$\rho_{\rm mass}=\varepsilon/c^2$ for every $c>0$; in the reduction notation
$r=\varepsilon$ solves $\partial_sr=-r\chi$ with the explicit exponential
solution of [[thm-gr-dust-local-evolution]]. For the fluid branch the strict
hypotheses $\epsilon+p>0$, $0<p'<1$ are essential; the failure at negative
$p'$ is the companion counterexample on the examples page. No statement is
made that any model here describes nature, and no empirical premise enters.

- **What is proved.** [[pthm-gr-linearized-field-equations]] derives the
  linearized field equation and its vacuum branch by differentiating the
  adopted field law [[post-gr-einstein-field-law]] along a smooth family of
  exact solutions. Its separate quadratic residual bound follows from the
  mathematical Taylor estimate for the Einstein tensor once
  $G^{(1)}(h)=0$; it does not require $\eta+\lambda h$ to belong to an exact
  solution family. The all-space harmonic-gauge existence clause additionally
  assumes $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. The mathematical
  existence statement for the vacuum plane waves is
  [[thm-gr-tt-plane-wave-solutions]]: for every pair of bounded smooth
  profiles there is an exact solution of the linearized vacuum equations in
  harmonic gauge, whose exact metric in the zero-source, $\Lambda=0$ branch
  has vacuum field-law residual bounded by a constant times the square of the
  amplitude on nonempty compact sets. [[pthm-gr-plane-wave-polarizations]] reads the amplitude
  classification of [[lem-gr-plane-wave-gauge-decomposition]] as the
  statement that the model has two polarization types at fixed null wave covector,
  with the gauge-invariant first-order curvature coefficients as their
  geometric content; no operational observable is defined on this page.
  [[pthm-gr-plane-wave-tidal-detector-response]] derives the model's
  infinitesimal relative-acceleration law for a geodesic variation and the
  finite path-length strain of the ideal two-body detector of
  [[def-gr-linearized-wave-regime-and-detector-coupling]].

- **What is conditional.** Every physical statement on the page is a
  deduction from the adopted postulates of
  [[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]],
  [[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]],
  [[post-gr-einstein-field-law]] and
  [[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]], together with the explicit
  hypotheses of the mathematical items. The postulates are adopted model
  assumptions, not derived results; no item on the page establishes the
  postulates, and no item compares a prediction with a measurement. For a TT perturbation the metric family $\eta+\lambda h$ satisfies the
  zero-source, $\Lambda=0$ equation through first order; its residual is
  bounded by $O(\lambda^2)$ on nonempty compact sets for sufficiently small
  amplitudes. This estimate does not establish an exact vacuum solution for
  nonzero $\lambda$. The admitted case $h=0$ is exactly flat and solves that
  equation for every $\lambda$. The polarization and response statements
  retain their stated linearized-model interpretation.

- **What is defined.** For a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field $T$
  and a smooth observer congruence $n$, the page defines the measured energy
  density, energy-momentum current, energy flux and spatial stress
  ([[def-gr-observer-energy-momentum-current]]), their physical reading and
  units ([[def-gr-measured-energy-density-flux-and-stress]]), the acceleration
  and expansion of the congruence
  ([[def-gr-congruence-acceleration-and-expansion]]), and, for a model with an
  everywhere timelike future-directed Killing field, the Killing current and
  the Killing charge of a finite three-chain (read as an energy in joules when
  the field is length-normalized under the framework's length-coordinate
  convention)
  ([[def-gr-killing-energy-charge]]). The algebraic decomposition behind the
  measured fields is proved in
  [[lem-gr-observer-energy-momentum-decomposition]], and the divergence and
  finite-chain identities in
  [[lem-gr-energy-momentum-current-divergence]] and
  [[lem-gr-killing-congruence-kinematics-and-energy-current]].

- **Smooth and finite branch.** All items assume smooth fields on an open
  domain and finite smooth singular chains; distributional sources,
  interfaces, noncompact or rough regions and asymptotic limits are outside
  the branch, in the sense of
  [[rem-gr-einstein-matter-scope-and-conventions]]. The observer congruence is
  an idealization of a family of ideal-clock worldlines; the physical reading
  of measured quantities is the framework's reading of
  [[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]], and no numerical value is
  asserted by any item of the page.

- **The curvature is the second-order obstruction.** The point-normal formula
  of [[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]] clause (c)
  expresses the curvature at the point through the second derivatives of the
  metric in any point-normal chart, and the curvature is a tensor field, so
  its vanishing is chart-independent
  ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). If the curvature
  vanishes on a normal neighborhood, the exponential chart is flat to all
  orders: the exponential map is an isometry onto an open subset of
  Minkowski space
  ([[thm-gr-vanishing-curvature-implies-locally-minkowski]] clauses (a)-(d)).
  This is the exact sense in which a flat metric is *locally* Minkowski.

- **Global Minkowski geometry is strictly stronger.** Vanishing curvature on
  a manifold does not determine its topology, its holonomy or its causal
  structure. The companion examples page exhibits a flat
  Lorentzian quotient of Minkowski space by a translation whose time
  coordinate is periodic: the metric is flat, the Einstein tensor vanishes,
  yet the manifold is not diffeomorphic to $\mathbb R^4$, admits closed
  timelike curves, and carries no global inertial chart; the theorem above is
  local precisely because it uses a normal neighborhood, not the whole
  manifold. Statements such as "the flat model is the spacetime" therefore
  require additional global hypotheses (simple connectedness, completeness,
  injectivity of the exponential map, a global chart) that are not part of
  the local computations of this page.

**(a) The deduction is conditional on the adopted postulates.** The
existence and uniqueness of the maximal development is a logical consequence
of [[post-gr-einstein-field-law]],
[[post-gr-spacetime-and-classical-domain]],
[[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]] and the mathematical theorem
[[thm-gr-smooth-maximal-globally-hyperbolic-development]], applied to data
that satisfy the constraints, complete-data regularity and actual local existence/geometric uniqueness/restart hypotheses of the fixed admissible coupled model in [[def-gr-development-and-data-fixing-isometry]]. Countable Choice and Dependent Choice are mathematical premises. The vacuum, scalar, strict-fluid and nonnegative tilted geodesic dust branches of [[thm-gr-high-regularity-selected-matter-development]] are included, with independently prescribed dust velocity through zero density; the conclusion is not confined to those four models and does not follow from an arbitrary conserved stress tensor.
Granting the postulates, the deduction is a theorem about the model; it is
not evidence that the model describes nature.

- **Observer dependence of measured energy.** The measured energy density
  $\mu=T_{ab}n^an^b$ and the SI measured energy flux $q=c\Phi$ of
  [[def-gr-measured-energy-density-flux-and-stress]] depend on the observer
  congruence $n$; only the tensor $T$ itself is observer independent. For a
  prescribed model different congruences generally assign different energies
  to the same region, and the framework contains no congruence-independent
  local energy density of matter.

- **No local gravitational energy in the framework as built.** The framework
  defines a stress-energy tensor only for the matter sector
  ([[def-gr-stress-energy-tensor-field]],
  [[post-gr-field-and-matter-assumptions]]): $T$ is the matter content of the
  field law, and the geometric side $G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}$ has identically
  vanishing divergence ([[thm-gr-second-bianchi-and-divergence-free-einstein]]).
  The local balance of [[pthm-gr-local-energy-balance]] is a balance of the
  *matter* current; no item of the framework defines a local gravitational
  energy density or flux that would complete it into a conservation law for a
  total energy. The framework's normal-coordinate material
  ([[thm-gr-point-normal-and-exponential-coordinate-charts]],
  [[rem-gr-normal-coordinates-and-local-inertial-frames-scope]]) records that
  the connection can be made to vanish at a point by an adapted chart while
  the curvature data cannot be removed by that choice; this is recorded here
  only as the scope statement that no construction of a local gravitational
  energy density is available from the connection alone. It is not a no-go
  theorem, and no no-go theorem is claimed. The cited treatments record the
  corresponding physical point: a gauge-invariant local energy density of the
  linearized gravitational field is unavailable, and gravitational energy
  cannot be localized.

- **A global energy needs a symmetry and control of the flux.** The Killing
  charge $Q_\xi$ of [[def-gr-killing-energy-charge]] exists only for a model
  that admits an everywhere timelike future-directed Killing field $\xi$;
  the theorem is conditional on this field and supplies no existence result
  for any specified metric ([[def-gr-killing-field]]). Even with such a
  $\xi$, the finite-chain
  statement of [[pthm-gr-local-energy-balance]] gives
  $Q_\xi(\Sigma_2)-Q_\xi(\Sigma_1)=-Q_\xi(B)$: conservation requires the side
  flux to vanish. It is read as an energy in joules when $\xi$ is
  length-normalized under the framework's length-coordinate convention; for
  another flow-parameter normalization, its units carry that scale. For a
  slice of unbounded spatial extent one further needs
  the limiting flux and the integrals to converge; the flux theorem
  [[thm-gr-density-divergence-and-finite-chain-flux]] is stated for finite
  smooth singular chains and supplies no such limit, and the framework's scope
  note [[rem-gr-einstein-matter-scope-and-conventions]] already excludes
  arbitrary rough or noncompact domains from its smooth branch.

4. *Perihelion advance.* Measurements of the residual precession of an
   almost-elliptical planetary orbit after the perturbations of the other
   bodies and the precession of the equinoxes have been modelled and removed,
   analysed over long astrometric baselines (Will section 4.2; Carroll
   (7.56)-(7.57)). The interface readout is the perihelion-advance readout of
   clause (b)4. Model-side content: the restricted Schwarzschild page supplies
   circular-orbit and photon-sphere predictions only
   (`pthm-gr-schwarzschild-circular-orbit-predictions`); a prediction of the
   advance of an eccentric orbit is a future obligation.

The exterior datum of [[def-gr-schwarzschild-exterior-model]] is defined on the
open domain $r>s$ only. At every point of this domain a product-chart frame
remains a basis. The component $g_{11}=f(r)^{-1}=(1-s/r)^{-1}$ diverges as
$r\downarrow s$, and the chart contains no point with $r=s$, so there is no
frame limit there in this chart. This is a statement about one component, not
an invariant: the metric tensor is smooth and nondegenerate on $r>s$ and has
the separate regular extension of [[lem-gr-schwarzschild-extension-chart]].

[[lem-gr-schwarzschild-extension-chart]] constructs on
$M_{\mathrm{ext}}=\mathbb R\times(0,\infty)\times S^2$ a smooth nondegenerate
Lorentzian metric $g_{\mathrm{ext}}$ whose restriction to $r>s$ is the exterior
datum; the level set $r=s$ is a smooth null hypersurface with generator
direction $\partial_v$, and the Ricci tensor and Kretschmann scalar of
$g_{\mathrm{ext}}$ extend smoothly across it. In the Kruskal model
([[def-gr-kruskal-model-data]], [[lem-gr-kruskal-model-properties]]) the same
surface appears as the axes $U=0$ or $V=0$: both are null surfaces of the
smooth metric $g_{\mathcal K}$, through which $r$ extends smoothly on all of
$\mathcal K$, and the curvature invariant $12s^2/r^6$ equals $12/s^4$ there.
The one-way character of the surface in the model is the exact statement of
[[lem-gr-kruskal-causal-escape-and-trapping]] clause (d): no future-directed
causal curve issued at a point with $U\ge0$ reaches the quadrant
$\{U<0,V>0\}$ with $r\to+\infty$, while every point with $U<0$ admits such a
curve along the future radial null geodesic at constant $U$. This is a causal
property of the smooth model; it is not a divergence of the metric at the
surface, and the model's time orientation is part of the datum.

The Kretschmann scalar of the exterior datum is
$K=R_{abcd}R^{abcd}=12s^2/r^6=\frac{48G_N^2m_*^2}{c^4r^6}$
([[lem-gr-schwarzschild-curvature-and-kretschmann-scalar]] clause (c)): on
$r>s$ it takes values in $(0,12/s^4)$ and has the finite boundary value
$12/s^4$ as $r\downarrow s$; on the smooth extension of
[[lem-gr-schwarzschild-extension-chart]], whose domain has $r>0$ and on which
the same expression $12s^2/r^6$ is the Kretschmann scalar, it grows without
bound as $r\downarrow0$. In the Kruskal model it is smooth on
$\mathcal K$ and grows without bound as $UV\to1$, that is, as $r\downarrow0$
([[lem-gr-kruskal-model-properties]] clause (d)). The value $r=0$ is not
attained on $\mathcal K$; the set $\{UV=1\}$ is not part of the model. The
invariant is a scalar built from the metric, so it is chart-independent, and
the following argument shows that $r=0$ cannot be appended as a regular
$C^2$ metric boundary point: if a $C^2$ Lorentzian metric on a manifold
containing $\mathcal K$ together with a boundary point $q$ approached with
$r\to0$ restricted to $g_{\mathcal K}$ on $\mathcal K$, then its curvature
tensor would be continuous near $q$ and its Kretschmann scalar bounded there,
contradicting the unboundedness of the same invariant along sequences in
$\mathcal K$. The distinction between the two values of $r$ is therefore a
statement about the smooth curvature of the model, not about the chosen
coordinates.

- **The model.** [[def-gr-schwarzschild-exterior-model]] fixes the datum: the
  manifold $\mathbb R\times(s,\infty)\times S^2$, the global smooth metric
  $g=-f\,d(x^0)^2+f^{-1}dr^2+r^2\gamma_{S^2}$ with diagonal components
  $-f,f^{-1},r^2,r^2\sin^2\vartheta$ in spherical-polar product charts, the
  time orientation $\partial_0$ and the parameters $c,G_N,m_*>0$ with
  $s=2G_Nm_*/c^2$. The components carry the unit readings of
  [[def-gr-si-unit-and-coordinate-conventions]]; no numerical value of any
  constant is asserted.
- **The vacuum calculation.** [[lem-gr-schwarzschild-ricci-and-einstein-tensors]]
  computes the Christoffel symbols, the curvature, the vanishing Ricci and
  Einstein tensors and the nonvanishing curvature of the datum, and
  [[pthm-gr-schwarzschild-vacuum-model]] reads the result as a model of the
  framework's field law with $T=0$ and $\Lambda=0$, together with the model's
  static clock readings and the reading of the mass parameter.
- **Local uniqueness.** [[thm-gr-local-birkhoff-warped-product]] shows that a
  vacuum warped product with spherical orbits is locally of this form with an
  extra local Killing field, under the explicit hypotheses of that theorem;
  the conclusion is local and does not assert that every vacuum solution or
  every spherical vacuum region is an exterior region with positive mass.
- **Restricted predictions.** [[pthm-gr-schwarzschild-stationary-redshift]]
  and [[pthm-gr-schwarzschild-circular-orbit-predictions]] are conditional
  model predictions for ideal clocks, test bodies and light rays, using the
  adopted coupling rules of [[post-gr-ideal-clocks-and-free-fall]]; they are
  not measurements and involve no apparatus model. The horizon and singularity
  distinctions are recorded in [[rem-gr-schwarzschild-horizon-and-singularity]].

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, $\kappa>0$ and one smooth EOS $p=p(\epsilon)$ on an open interval $J$ with $\epsilon+p>0$ and $0<p'(\epsilon)<1$ ([[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]). Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold with smooth metric $h$, symmetric tensor $K_2$, density $\epsilon_0:\Sigma\to J$ and tangent field $v_0$ with $h(v_0,v_0)<1$. These specify the future unit initial velocity
$$U_0=W_0(N+v_0),\qquad W_0=(1-h(v_0,v_0))^{-1/2}$$
in $\mathcal V=\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$, with metric $g_0(aN+X,bN+Y)=-ab+h(X,Y)$. Require the constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] for
$$T_0=(\epsilon_0+p(\epsilon_0))U_0^{\flat_{g_0}}\otimes U_0^{\flat_{g_0}}+p(\epsilon_0)g_0.$$
Then a smooth time-oriented local development has metric $g$, density $\epsilon$ and future unit fluid velocity $u$ satisfying
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\left[(\epsilon+p)u_au_b+pg_{ab}\right],\qquad D\epsilon+(\epsilon+p)\vartheta=0,\qquad (\epsilon+p)a^b+\Pi^{ba}\partial_ap=0.$$
Here $D=\nabla_u$, $\vartheta=\nabla_a u^a$, $a=\nabla_u u$ and $\Pi^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^au^b$. Initial geometric data are $(h,K_2)$ and initial matter data are $(\epsilon_0,U_0)$ under $N\mapsto n$, $X\mapsto i_*X$. Arbitrary smooth subluminal tilt is allowed. The initial surface lies in the interior of its intrinsic domain of dependence; its interior Cauchy neighborhood is globally hyperbolic. Any two developments of this same EOS and complete data agree near the entire initial surface by a data-fixing future isometry matching density and velocity. The neighborhood may have position-dependent time width; shocks, vacuum boundaries and vanishing sound speed are outside this strict interior-fluid statement ([[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]).
[L3] The constraints are the geometric normal residuals for exactly the initial stress displayed above ([[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]], [[def-gr-perfect-fluid-matter-model]]).

A timelike initial velocity is specified in the abstract Lorentz bundle over the Riemannian surface; it is not an intrinsic timelike vector of its tangent bundle. No small-tilt restriction or uniform noncompact width is required.

**(c)** for all $p,q\in M$ the causal diamond
$J^+(p)\cap J^-(q)$ is compact; consequently $(M,g,N)$ is globally
hyperbolic in the sense of clause (c) of that definition.

[L3] Two-endpoint limit curve theorem. For future causal curves $\alpha_k:[0,b_k]\to M$ parametrized by $h$-arclength with $\alpha_k(0)\to x$, $\alpha_k(b_k)\to z$ and $b:=\lim_kb_k$ finite, if $b>0$ then the common-domain reparametrizations $\widetilde\alpha_k(t)=\alpha_k((b_k/b)t)$ on $[0,b]$ have a subsequence converging uniformly to a future causal curve $\alpha:[0,b]\to M$ from $x$ to $z$; if $b=0$ then $x=z$ and the uniform limit is the constant map. If $x=z$ and $b>0$, the limit is nonconstant. If $b=\infty$, there are a future-inextendible future causal curve $\alpha^+:[0,\infty)\to M$ and a past-inextendible future causal curve $\alpha^-:(-\infty,0]\to M$ with $\alpha^+(0)=x$ and $\alpha^-(0)=z$ such that for all $t_+\ge0,t_-\le0$ there are event pairs $u_k,v_k\in M$ with $u_k\le v_k$, $u_k\to\alpha^+(t_+)$ and $v_k\to\alpha^-(t_-)$ ([[thm-gr-limit-curve-two-endpoints]] clauses (i)-(iii), [[lem-gr-basic-limit-curve]]). Every finite future causal curve can be reparametrized by $h$-arclength as established in Step 1.2 of [[lem-gr-basic-limit-curve]].

[L6] The metric $h$ is a complete Riemannian metric on each connected component and its distance $d_h$ induces the manifold topology; closed $d_h$-bounded sets are compact ([[thm-gr-auxiliary-complete-riemannian-metric]] clauses (c) and (d), [[thm-the-riemannian-distance-topology-is-the-manifold-topology]], [[thm-riemannian-distance-is-a-metric]]). The $h$-arclength of a future causal curve satisfies $d_h(\gamma(s),\gamma(t))\le\ell_h(\gamma|_{[s,t]})$ for $s<t$ by the same reasoning as [[lem-gr-basic-limit-curve]].

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$, curvature tensors
$R^{a}{}_{bcd}$, $\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$, scalar curvature $S$ and Einstein
tensor $G_{ab}$ ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]],
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
